name: batch-job
description: A scheduled or triggered batch engine with no web API: a CLI run by a scheduler, with inputs, outputs, a schedule and an audit trail rather than a port or a route.

runtimes.provision: <installed on the host that runs it; a per-app virtual environment>

runtimes.kind: <other, e.g. a native library or a licensed asset the job depends on>
runtimes.provision: <provisioned separately; licensed assets come from their licensed source, never from version control>

schedule.trigger: <a task scheduler, a file-arrival watcher, or a manual/CI trigger>
schedule.account: <a service account, never a person's own login>
schedule.command: <the CLI entry point, e.g. python -m <package> run>
schedule.overlap: <what happens if a run is still going when the next one is due>

config.rule: kept out of version control; a committed example file

data.state: <input, staging and output locations, kept outside the repo; a retention rule; never committed, especially real customer data>

ci.workflow: <CI workflow file: lint, tests, a dry run against sanitised sample data>
ci.deployJob: <deploy_prod (updates code and dependencies; does not itself run a batch)>

deploy.script: <deploy script: stop the schedule, update, re-enable; never mid-run>
verify: a dry run against sanitised sample data exits zero and writes the expected output artefact
the next scheduled run completes and writes its expected output artefact
